summary: Describes how to use Frame Relay for framing PPP packets. It is on the standards track as a proposed standard.

eli5.summary: It shows how to carry the dial-up link protocol over a different kind of wide-area service, by putting packets in the right wrapper.

questions: how to run ppp over frame relay
what is ppp in frame relay
can ppp and hdlc share a frame relay link
subtitle: How to use Frame Relay frames as the wrapper for PPP on a point-to-point circuit.

tldr.problem: PPP normally uses HDLC-like framing, but Frame Relay links need PPP packets carried in Frame Relay frames, and the two framing styles cannot share a link.
tldr.mechanism: PPP packets are wrapped in a Frame Relay header with NLPID value 0xcf, and the first octet after the header tells a receiver whether the frame is PPP or an ordinary Multiprotocol Interconnect encapsulation.
tldr.outcome: PPP features such as LCP, NCPs, authentication and compression become usable over point-to-point Frame Relay circuits. It is a Proposed Standard with no recorded replacement.

facts.label: Network-layer MTU limit
facts.value: 1500 unless peer MRU is 2048 or greater

facts.label: LCP packet limit on small switches

today: RFC 1973 is a Proposed Standard published in June 1996, and the unit metadata records no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It builds on RFC 1661 (PPP) and RFC 1490.

sections.title: Introduction and Scope
sections.content:
Frame Relay, like X.25, provides virtual circuits between stations attached to the same network. It is simpler than X.25 because Q.922 only delivers packets and dispenses with sequencing and flow control. When Frame Relay is configured as a point-to-point circuit, PPP can use it purely as a framing mechanism and ignore its other features.

This is meant for implementations that want PPP facilities such as the Link Control Protocol (LCP), Network-layer Control Protocols (NCPs), authentication and compression. These need a point-to-point relationship, so the specification is not designed for multi-point or multi-access environments.

The RFC notes that PPP in HDLC-like frames and Frame Relay were once expected to co-exist on the same links, but the Q.922 address expansion method cannot be told apart from the ISO 3309 method, so co-existence is precluded.
sections.eli5: Frame Relay already knows how to move envelopes between two places. PPP just uses those envelopes and ignores the fancier mail services.

sections.title: Physical Layer Requirements
sections.content:
PPP treats Frame Relay framing as a bit-synchronous link. The link MUST be full-duplex but MAY be either dedicated (permanent) or switched. PPP presents an octet interface to the physical layer and puts no limit on transmission rate beyond what the Frame Relay interface itself has.

Frame Relay needs control signals that say when the link is connected or disconnected, and these supply the Up and Down events to the LCP state machine. Since PPP does not normally need control signals, their failure MUST NOT affect correct operation of PPP. Frame Relay requires NRZ encoding, while other encodings are the job of the DTE/DCE equipment.
sections.eli5: The wire has to carry traffic both ways at once. If the wire's signal lights fail, PPP should keep working anyway.

sections.title: The Frame Format
sections.content:
The framing follows the Multiprotocol Interconnect over Frame Relay specification (RFC 1490). The Q.922 header address and control fields are combined with the Network Layer Protocol Identifier (NLPID), which identifies the encapsulation that follows. A frame starts with the flag 0x7e, then the Q.922 address, control, the NLPID (0xcf for PPP) and the PPP Protocol field. The Protocol, Information and Padding fields are as in RFC 1661.

LCP can negotiate changes to the basic frame, but modified frames stay distinguishable from standard ones. Address-and-Control-Field-Compression MUST NOT be negotiated, because the Address and Control values are not constant and change as the network switches the frame. Protocol-Field-Compression SHOULD be negotiated when it helps throughput: unlike HDLC-like framing, Frame Relay does not align the Information field on a 32-bit boundary, but removing the NLPID and compressing the Protocol field to one octet does.
sections.eli5: Every PPP message gets a label saying 'this is PPP', and the label can be shortened to make everything line up neatly in memory. The parts of the address that the network changes along the way must not be squeezed out.

sections.title: In-Band Protocol Demultiplexing
sections.content:
The PPP NLPID (0xcf) plus the PPP Protocol field distinguish PPP from the other NLPID encapsulations. Joining the number spaces also lets LCP Protocol-Reject report NLPIDs that are not recognized, which avoids black holes. Where a network protocol has no PPP assignment or has not been negotiated by an NCP, another encapsulation from RFC 1490 SHOULD be used.

On receipt, the first octet after the header is examined. If it is zero, the packet MUST be treated as RFC 1490 format. PPP packets always have a non-zero octet there. If it is not 0xcf, Protocol-Field-Compression is enabled and the NCP is negotiated, it is a compressed Protocol value; otherwise it is treated as RFC 1490 format. The Protocol value 0x00cf is reserved to avoid ambiguity.

Initial LCP packets contain cf-c0-21 after the header, and a recognized Configure-Request moves the link into Link Establishment phase. In that phase other NLPID values MUST NOT be sent, and received ones MUST be silently discarded until the Network-Layer Protocol phase. Once an NCP is up, a frame in another equivalent encapsulation forces the link back to Link Establishment with a new Configure-Request, preventing black holes if the peer lost state. If configuration fails, an implementation MAY enter Termination phase; otherwise at the Max-Configure limit it MUST fall back to sending only RFC 1490 frames.

Accidentally feeding a multipoint network SHOULD cause a misconfiguration indication, detectable by multiple responses to one Configure-Request Identifier from different framing addresses. There is no agreed out-of-band signalling method, so implementations MUST use in-band demultiplexing for both permanent and switched virtual circuits.
sections.eli5: When a message arrives, the receiver peeks at the first byte to decide whether it is a PPP message or an older kind of message. If the sender and receiver lose track of each other, they start the conversation over.

sections.title: Configuration Details
sections.content:
The recommended LCP options are Magic Number and Protocol Field Compression. Standard LCP defaults apply, except for the Maximum-Receive-Unit (MRU). To stay interoperable with existing Frame Relay implementations the initial MRU is 1600 octets, which only sets the minimum buffer space for receiving, not the size of packets sent.

To avoid fragmentation, the network-layer MTU SHOULD NOT exceed 1500 unless a peer MRU of 2048 or greater is negotiated. Some switches only handle 262 octet frames; deploying one that handles fewer than 1600 octets is not recommended, but implementations MUST be configurable to limit LCP packets to 259 octets until LCP negotiation is complete. XID negotiation and Inverse ARP are not required, since PPP NCP negotiation provides that function.
sections.eli5: Both ends start by agreeing on a box size big enough for most messages. Very small boxes in the network are tolerated only while they set things up.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC states only that security issues are not discussed in the memo. PPP authentication is named in the applicability statement as one of the PPP facilities this framing makes available, but this document defines nothing about it.
sections.eli5: This note does not say anything about keeping messages secret or safe.
